issues.legal_issue: A finding that a passage formed part of an oral tenancy is reviewable in a second appeal when it rests on an inference that cannot legally be drawn from the proved facts.
material_facts: The tenancy was created orally, with no document describing its subject matter.

The lower appellate court inferred that the passage formed part of the tenancy from the tenants’ use of the building’s street address, their signboard, and the passage being the only route then used to reach their premises.
The passage was also used in common by the owner and several tenants.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could review the lower appellate court’s conclusion because the issue was not purely factual; the inference that the passage formed part of the tenancy could not legally be drawn from the proved facts.
issues.legal_principle: Whether proved facts support a legal conclusion may be a question concerning the propriety of that conclusion rather than a purely factual finding. The Court relied on no cited provision or earlier case.

predicates.second_appeal: The matter came before the High Court in a second appeal.
predicates.lower_finding_based_on_inference: The lower appellate court reached its finding by inferring a fact from other proved circumstances.
predicates.proved_facts_do_not_support_inference: The circumstances proved in the case did not legally support the inference drawn by the lower appellate court.

issues.definition: When a second appeal challenges a finding inferred from proved circumstances that do not support it, the High Court may interfere with that finding.

issues.legal_issue: Use of a common passage to reach leased premises does not make the passage part of the tenancy when the circumstances relied on establish access but not inclusion in the demise.
material_facts: The tenancy was created orally and there was no document describing its subject matter.
The tenants used the building’s street address in correspondence and advertisements and displayed a signboard on the street frontage.
The disputed passage was the only passage then used to reach the first-floor premises, but it was also used by the owner and several tenants to reach their respective portions of the building.
issues.conclusion: The passage was not part of the tenants’ demise and was not an essential element of their tenancy; the circumstances established access to the premises, not that the passage itself was leased to them.
issues.legal_principle: An address shared by occupants of a building, a signboard, and use of a route do not establish that a common passage formed part of a particular tenant’s demise where the passage was used by the owner and other tenants as well. The Court relied on no cited provision or earlier case.

predicates.oral_tenancy: The landlord and tenant created the tenancy orally without a document identifying the passage as part of the leased premises.
predicates.passage_used_in_common: The owner and multiple tenants used the passage to reach their respective portions of the building.
predicates.evidence_shows_access_but_not_inclusion_: The circumstances showed that the tenant used the passage for access but did not establish that the passage was included in the tenancy.

issues.definition: When an oral tenancy and common use of a passage are accompanied only by evidence of the tenant’s access, the passage is not part of the tenancy.

issues.legal_issue: An easement of necessity to use a disputed passage does not arise when alternative access to the retained premises is available, even if that access is less convenient or advantageous.
material_facts: The owner conveyed part of the property without reserving the disputed passage and permitted structures to be built on the conveyed portion.
The owner provided the tenants with alternative access to their premises through another street.
The tenants claimed a right to continue using the disputed passage as an easement of necessity.
issues.conclusion: The tenants had no easement of necessity over the disputed passage because alternative access was available; its lesser convenience or advantage was irrelevant.
issues.legal_principle: An easement of necessity requires necessity for access, not merely a more convenient or advantageous route. The Court relied on no cited provision or earlier case.

predicates.easement_of_necessity_claim: A party claimed a right to use a route as an easement of necessity.
predicates.property_severed: Ownership of part of a property was transferred, leaving another part retained.
predicates.alternative_access_available: The party had another route providing access to the retained premises.

issues.definition: When property has been severed but another route provides access, a claim to use the disputed route as an easement of necessity fails.

issues.legal_issue: Common use of a passage does not establish a granted easement where no grant was pleaded or supported by evidence.
material_facts: The tenants argued that the passage was used under an easement of right of way granted to them and other tenants.
They had not made that case in the courts below, and the record contained no material from which a grant could be inferred.
The passage had been used in common by the owner and the tenants to access their respective premises.
issues.conclusion: The claimed granted easement was not established; the common use showed a bare licence to use the passage for access, without an interest in it.
issues.legal_principle: A grant of an easement cannot be inferred without a pleaded case and supporting material; common use by the owner and tenants may instead show a bare licence that creates no interest in the passage. The Court relied on no cited provision or earlier case.

rule.if: granted_easement_claim and claim_not_raised_below and no_evidence_of_grant and passage_used_in_common

predicates.granted_easement_claim: A party claimed that a right to use a passage had been granted as an easement.
predicates.claim_not_raised_below: The party did not advance the granted-easement claim in the lower courts.
predicates.no_evidence_of_grant: The record contained no material showing that an easement had been granted.
predicates.passage_used_in_common: The owner and multiple occupants used the passage to reach their respective premises.

issues.definition: A claimed granted easement is not established when it was not raised below and has no evidentiary support, while common use of the passage amounts only to a bare licence.
